title: MonetaPay POC scoping - workload modeling
next_steps: Send preliminary benchmark spreadsheet and QPS/concurrency template
Schedule 2-hour on-prem/Dedicated perf test for week of 7/20
Share security brief (SOC2 + KMS integration) and SSO instructions
Provide cost estimate for 3-month POC (dedicated commit + hosted fallback)
action_items: Samantha: Share benchmark template + sample workload by 2026-07-08
Liam: Prepare perf test plan + infra checklist by 2026-07-13
Rajesh: Provide representative traffic logs / 2 weeks of request traces by 2026-07-10
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling for MonetaPay: discussed QPS and concurrency targets, input/output token distribution, latency SLOs, benchmarks to run on Redwood Dedicated vs hosted, timeline for 3-month POC and next steps for performance testing and security docs.
questions: What are your peak vs average QPS?
What percent of requests need sub-second p95?
Any hard restrictions on data residency or on-prem requirement?
Do you have representative input/output token length distribution or sample requests?
transcript: 00:00:00 - Samantha Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, curious to get context on what you want to validate in this POC - hi Rajesh, Priya, Derek, Sara.

00:00:07 - Rajesh Kapoor: Thanks Sam, yes so MonetaPay wants to validate running our transaction classification and fraud scoring models with a real-time payment flow. Primary goals are latency, cost, and data isolation for european flows.

00:00:18 - Priya Nair: Just to add, our ML infra currently sends about 3 QPS on average for rule-based scoring but during peak promotions we've seen spikes up to 18-20 QPS. Most calls are short prompts — customer metadata + last 10 transactions, so input token distribution is usually 80-200 tokens, output around 30-120 tokens.
00:00:36 - Liam Chen: Got it, that's helpful. When you say 18-20 QPS spikes, what's the concurrency at your service boundary? Like how many concurrent requests do you have during those spikes?

00:00:45 - Derek Miles: We see concurrency up to 40 concurrent requests because our frontend buffers and then fan outs to multiple scoring endpoints, but single-model path is usually 8-16 concurently handled at the scoring microservice.

00:00:55 - Samantha Ortiz: That's a useful distinction — fan-out vs single-model concurrency. For modeling POC capacity we'll look at both single-worker concurrency and aggregate QPS. Typical Redwood POCs set target steady-state QPS and simulated spike windows.

00:01:06 - Rajesh Kapoor: For success criteria: p95 latency under 400ms for the short requests (<=200 input tokens, output <=100), and end-to-end throughput that meets our 20 QPS burst with graceful degradation. Also need audit logs and KMS-backed encryption for payloads.
00:01:19 - Priya Nair: Another criterion is cost per thousand requests — we have an internal threshold, so part of the POC is to compare Dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted pay-as-you-go economics.
00:01:30 - Liam Chen: Understood. For the workload characterization, can you confirm percentiles of input length? E.g., p50, p75, p95 of input token length and output token length?
00:01:39 - Priya Nair: Rough numbers: input p50 ~110 tokens, p75 ~160, p95 ~380 (we have occasional long context when we send full conversation), output p50 ~45, p75 ~70, p95 ~180.

00:01:50 - Samantha Ortiz: Great — that will drive model choice and batching strategy. Quick note: if you have many short requests, continuous batching and prefix caching can reduce cost significantly; larger inputs constrain batching and memory footprint (KV cache).

00:02:02 - Derek Miles: On infra, we have VPC requirements for EU production; for the POC we can do a Dedicated in eu-west with private networking or a hosted route if we can't provision dedicated hardware immediately.

00:02:12 - Rajesh Kapoor: Ideally we'd test Dedicated, but if that's slow to provision we can start on hosted and move to Dedicated for the second phase. We want to see performance on our largest model candidate (13B quantized) and maybe compare a 7B variant.

00:02:23 - Liam Chen: That fits our recommended pattern — baseline on hosted to validate function, then Dedicated for sustained throughput and predictable unit economics. For the 13B quantized workloads we'll want to size GPU pools and measure p95 latency, token/s throughput, and memory paging behavior.
00:02:35 - Priya Nair: What tooling will you run for the benchmarks? We'll share traces but we need to ensure fidelity to our production traffic (headers, tokenization, routing).

00:02:43 - Samantha Ortiz: We'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet and a small runner that replays requests with your tokenization and timing distribution. It supports parameterization for QPS ramps, spikes, and concurrency profiles. Liam will prepare an infra checklist for Dedicated tests.

00:02:54 - Liam Chen: For metrics we'll capture per-request latency (client-to-client), model internal token generation time, GPU utilization, batch sizes, and tail latencies. Also will surface batching efficiency (tokens per batch) which drives cost. We'll include raw logs for KV cache hits/misses.

00:03:07 - Sara Gomez: One question: we have a synchronous endpoint in our payments flow where sub-second response is important — about 60% of requests need sub-second p95, the remaining can tolerate up to 2s. How does that map to SLA tiers or routing policies?

00:03:19 - Liam Chen: We typically recommend a routing policy that prefers low-latency variants (smaller models or more provisioned instances) for synchronous critical paths. Redwood supports routing by latency SLO and can fallback to a cheaper model for non-critical traffic. We'll model an A/B route during the POC.
00:03:30 - Rajesh Kapoor: For security, we need SOC2 evidence, audit logs, SSO via SAML, and KMS integration for key management. Any gotchas on that side?

00:03:38 - Samantha Ortiz: We'll send our security brief — Redwood Private and Dedicated support KMS/HSM integrations, SAML SSO, and audit logs. For POC you can opt-in to keep logs in your VPC or use a hashed payload approach if you need to limit exposure.
00:03:49 - Priya Nair: On metrics again — when you talk about tokens per batch, do you have heuristic numbers for 13B vs 7B on batch size and latency breakpoints?

00:03:58 - Liam Chen: Roughly: 7B models allow larger effective batch sizes before latency increases — you might get 6-10 concurrent requests batched efficiently on a T4/RTX class; 13B quantized will have smaller batch sweet spot and more memory pressure. We'll capture that in kernel-level benchmarks. But real numbers will depend on your seq length distribution — those p95 long inputs will reduce batching efficiency.
00:04:16 - Derek Miles: For Dedicated sizing, what capacity should we commit to for a 3-month POC that simulates production steady state of 3 QPS with 20 QPS spikes and concurrency up to 40?

00:04:25 - Liam Chen: For that pattern, a small Dedicated pool with autoscaling + burst capacity is typical. We'll propose a base capacity to handle steady 3 QPS at low-cost model variant and the ability to autoscale for spikes; exact GPUs depend on model and quantization — we'll size in the spreadsheet after we run initial perf runs.

00:04:37 - Samantha Ortiz: Success criteria recap: 1) p95 latency <400ms for short requests for the primary model variant, 2) smooth handling of 20 QPS burst with graceful degradation, 3) KMS + audit log proof-of-concept, 4) cost estimate within MonetaPay threshold. If all met we move to a 3-month pilot on Dedicated.
00:04:51 - Rajesh Kapoor: That sounds right. Timeline — we want to start tests week of 7/20 and have results by mid-August so stakeholders can review by end of August. Is that feasible?

00:04:59 - Liam Chen: Yes — typical timeline: week 1 (7/13) prep and config, week of 7/20 run hosted baseline tests, week of 7/27 run Dedicated perf runs, week of 8/3 analyze and iterate. We'll aim to have a runbook and data by 8/14.
00:05:11 - Priya Nair: We'll collect traces and an anonymized sample of 5k requests for replay. Expect that by 7/10.

00:05:17 - Samantha Ortiz: Perfect — that'll let us model token length distribution more precisely. One more thing: are you open to testing a smaller distilled model (7B) as a latency-optimized variant for synchronous paths?
00:05:25 - Rajesh Kapoor: Yes, if accuracy tradeoffs are acceptable. We'll want to see a quality comparison on a few hundred labeled examples as part of the POC.

00:05:32 - Liam Chen: We'll include quality evals tied to the benchmark harness — you can provide the labeled set and we'll run automated scoring and a small blind eval so you can inspect regressions.
00:05:40 - Sara Gomez: On instrumentation: we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards. Can Redwood surface those during the POC?

00:05:47 - Samantha Ortiz: Yes — Redwood Console will show token breakdowns by model/route, per-request latency, and we can surface a CSV with cost calc assumptions. We'll enable access for your team for the POC window.
00:05:55 - Priya Nair: Any limitations on private data? We have PCI-adjacent metadata — how do you handle that during hosted runs?

00:06:03 - Liam Chen: For PCI-adjacent data we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments. If you start hosted, we can hash or tokenize sensitive fields client-side. We'll include recommendations in the security brief.
00:06:11 - Rajesh Kapoor: Good. Last item: do you have examples of similar bank/fintech POCs and their typical batch sizes and cost outcomes?

00:06:20 - Samantha Ortiz: We can anonymize a few case studies — finance customers often trade model size for latency; switching to a quantized 13B can cut cost 30-40% vs non-quant, and using prefix caching for repeated account contexts can reduce tokens generated by ~25% in some flows. We'll add anonymized numbers to the welcome packet.
00:06:34 - Derek Miles: Ok we'll prioritize delivering traces and labeled examples by 7/10. Anything else on success criteria?
00:06:41 - Rajesh Kapoor: No, that's it from my side. Thanks — next step deliverables from Redwood and then schedule the perf window.
00:06:46 - Samantha Ortiz: Thanks everyone — recap in next steps in the follow-up. We'll share the benchmark spreadsheet now and confirm the test windows. End call.
00:06:51 - [call ends]
